source.title: Eight-week antidepressant treatment reduces functional connectivity in first-episode drug-naive patients with major depressive disorder.

confidence_rationale: Provides a chronicity/staging signal relevant to Q-061's RA-001 sub-question: a prior big-data finding (referenced and built on here) located abnormal DMN connectivity in RECURRENT but not first-episode drug-naive MDD, and this study shows antidepressants THEMSELVES reduce connectivity across networks -- so apparent 'abnormality' partly reflects medication, and the untreated first-episode regime may differ from the chronic/recurrent one. Mixed direction: supports a duration/staging-dependence of the regime while cautioning that medication confounds reversibility inferences.
failure_signatures: No significant DMN connectivity difference between treatment-naive first-episode patients and healthy controls -- the 'depressive regime' connectivity signature may be a property of recurrence/chronicity (or of medication), not of the acute first episode, which would reframe what 'reversal' even targets early vs late.
Widespread connectivity REDUCTION caused by antidepressants per se means treatment-related 'normalisation' can be a medication artefact rather than true regime repair.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Abnormal intrinsic DMN connectivity was reported in recurrent but not first-episode drug-naive MDD; in this study eight weeks of antidepressants reduced connectivity across most networks, and no connectivity difference was found between treatment-naive first-episode patients and controls, indicating antidepressant effects must be disentangled from MDD pathophysiology.
mapping.ree_translation: Bears on Q-061's duration-dependence (RA-001): the network regime signature appears tied to recurrence/chronicity rather than the acute episode, consistent with the hypothesis that early and late depressive regimes are not the same object and may demand different repair routes. Also a methodological caution for how REE interprets 'normalisation' as evidence of repair.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Cross-sectional staging contrast (first-episode vs recurrent) is inherited from the cited big-data study, not a within-subject longitudinal test of duration-locking; cannot establish that early-effective repair routes FAIL late, only that the regime's connectivity signature is stage-associated. Strong medication confound.
mapping.source_context: Human resting-state fMRI; 41 first-episode drug-naive MDD pre/post 8-week SSRI/SNRI, 92 matched controls; network-based and large-scale network analyses.

confidence_components.notes: Methodologically careful (isolates medication effects), but the chronicity inference is cross-sectional and the relevant first-episode-vs-recurrent contrast is partly carried over from the referenced big-data study.
